issues.legal_issue: General limitation rules governing extension and computation apply to appeals under a special revenue enactment when the applicable procedural law incorporates those rules and does not exclude them.
material_facts: The special enactment allowed an appeal to the revenue board within a fixed period but did not itself provide for excluding time spent obtaining a copy or condoning delay.
The special enactment made procedure under a revenue law applicable to proceedings and appeals.
The revenue law directed that general limitation rules apply, subject to specified provisions.
issues.conclusion: The limitation rules concerning computation and extension, including the applicable provisions of the Limitation Act, governed the appeal. The reference to extension of the “principles” of limitation was to be understood as referring to extension of the period of limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 30 and 29 of the Madhya Bharat Abolition of Jagirs Act, 1951, and sections 34 and 149(2) of the Ryotwari Land Revenue and Tenancy Act, Samwat 2007, the applicable limitation rules guided computation and extension of the appeal period. Section 149(2)'s reference to extension of the “principles” of limitation was construed as referring to extension of the period of limitation, consistently with Brijrajsingh v. The Board of Revenue. Sections 3, 4, 5 and 29(2) of the Limitation Act, 1908, showed that section 12 applied unless excluded; section 12 allowed time spent obtaining a copy to be excluded in computing limitation.

rule.if: revenue_appeal and revenue_procedure_applies and limitation_guidance_is_incorporated and not limitation_rules_expressly_excluded

predicates.revenue_appeal: A party brings an appeal to a revenue authority against a decision made under a special enactment.
predicates.revenue_procedure_applies: The special enactment makes procedural rules governing revenue proceedings applicable to the appeal.
predicates.limitation_guidance_is_incorporated: The applicable procedural law directs the decision-maker to follow general limitation rules for extension or computation.
predicates.limitation_rules_expressly_excluded: The applicable enactments expressly exclude the relevant general limitation rules.
predicates.limitation_computation_and_extension_rul: The decision-maker applies the relevant general rules for computing and extending the appeal period.

issues.definition: When a revenue appeal is governed by applicable revenue procedure that incorporates limitation guidance and does not expressly exclude the relevant rules, those rules apply to computation and extension of the appeal period.

issues.legal_issue: A revenue board may not reject an appeal as time-barred without excluding necessary time spent obtaining the reasons for the decision and considering whether any remaining delay should be condoned.
material_facts: The compensation memorandum communicated the amount awarded but did not disclose the basis of the calculation or how the claimant's claims had been addressed.
The claimant sought a copy of the reasoned decision the day after receiving the memorandum, promptly complied with the copying-fee requirement, and received the copy shortly afterward.
The claimant filed the appeal after the prescribed period if the time spent obtaining the copy was not excluded; the possible remaining delay was slight.
The revenue board rejected the appeal on limitation without considering exclusion of the copy-obtaining time or whether any remaining delay should be condoned.
issues.conclusion: The board's rejection was not judicial and had to be set aside. The matter was remitted for the appeal to be disposed of according to law, including consideration of limitation and any application to condone delay.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the Limitation Act, 1908, applied through sections 34 and 149(2) of the Ryotwari Act and allowed the time spent obtaining a copy of the judgment forming the basis of the decision to be excluded. Under section 5 of the Limitation Act, any remaining delay could be considered for condonation if sufficient cause was shown. The board was required to consider those matters rather than dismiss the appeal without doing so.

rule.if: revenue_appeal and decision_notice_omits_reasoned_basis and reasoned_copy_needed_to_frame_appeal and copy_sought_promptly and board_rejects_without_considering_copy_time_or_delay_cause

predicates.revenue_appeal: A party appeals to a revenue authority against a decision made under a special enactment.
predicates.decision_notice_omits_reasoned_basis: The notice communicating the decision does not disclose the reasoning or basis needed to understand how the decision was reached.
predicates.reasoned_copy_needed_to_frame_appeal: A copy of the reasoned decision is needed to formulate an effective appeal.
predicates.copy_sought_promptly: The appellant promptly requests the reasoned copy and promptly complies with any requirement to obtain it.
predicates.board_rejects_without_considering_copy_t: The appellate authority dismisses the appeal as late without addressing exclusion of time spent obtaining the copy or whether any remaining delay has sufficient cause.
predicates.limitation_rejection_must_be_set_aside_a: The dismissal on limitation is set aside and the appeal is returned for reconsideration according to law.

issues.definition: When a revenue appeal depends on a reasoned decision omitted from the notice, the appellant promptly seeks a copy, and the board rejects the appeal without considering the copy-obtaining time or the cause of any remaining delay, the rejection must be set aside and the appeal reconsidered.
